CraftaxClassic.parity_note: Measured on 64 sampled states at 7 px and 16 px, over the WHOLE observation -- the 7x9 world window and the 2-row inventory strip -- and over the whole day cycle: 18 night rows (light_level < 0.5, noise field drawn), 29 dusk rows (0.5 <= light < 1, lit but noise-free) and 17 daylight rows, sleeping rows throughout. Against craftax 1.6.1 under jax 0.11.1 with jax_threefry_partitionable at its default True: 100% of all pixels exact in every band, max abs diff 0. The claim is a UINT8 claim and deliberately not a float one, because the reference does not have one float value to be equal to: under jax.jit XLA fuses its arithmetic differently and it disagrees with its own un-jitted self by up to 1.5e-05, which is invisible in uint8 by day and visible wherever the picture is compressed towards one value, which the sleep desaturation and the night blend both do. Against the JITTED reference this renderer is 99.7854% (7 px) and 99.7225% (16 px) of pixels exact with max abs diff 1 ON THIS POOL, where every differing pixel was on a sleeping row; independent review found the jitted reference differing on an awake row at light_level 0.49999997, so any LIT row can straddle and the sleeping rows are only the commonest case. reference_env therefore returns the un-jitted function, which is the renderer as written. jax is a declared reference version because jax_threefry_partitionable selects between two threefry counter layouts that agree on 0 of 448 draws, and the night noise field is drawn from one of them.

certification_state_distribution.band_assignment: stratified by row index (i % 6); values inside a band from craftax's own day cycle and light-map alphabet
certification_state_distribution.note: a row stays on the uint8 gather only if it is fully lit AND awake AND at unit gain, so the fast-path share is NOT the 2/6 the lighting bands alone give: the sleeping stratification (i % 4 == 3) takes a quarter of them away and the answer is 0.25. The two level-0 night bands are the only ones that draw the threefry field. The LIGHTING shares are exact when the batch is a multiple of six and otherwise move by the remainder: at the certification batch of 64 the night share measures 0.328 against 1/3, while the fast-path share is exactly 0.25 at that batch

CraftaxFull.parity_note: Measured on the frozen Step-7 corpus at 10 px (the registered observation) and 16 px, over the WHOLE observation -- the 9x11 world window and the 4-row inventory strip -- and over all five cost bands: level 0 at full daylight, level 0 at dusk, level 0 at night (the noise field drawn), levels 1-8 fully lit, and levels 1-8 in darkness, with sleeping rows throughout. Against craftax 1.6.1 under jax 0.11.1 with jax_threefry_partitionable at its default True and do_night_noise at its default True: 100% of all pixels exact, max abs diff 0. The claim is a UINT8 claim and deliberately not a float one, because the reference does not have one float value to be equal to: under jax.jit XLA fuses its arithmetic differently and it disagrees with its own un-jitted self by up to 1.53e-05, which is invisible in uint8 on a fully lit frame and not invisible wherever the picture is compressed towards one value -- which the light_map multiply, the night blend and the sleep halving all do. On a 49-state phase-0 pool 48 of 49 jitted frames were uint8-identical to the un-jitted ones and one differed on 0.0023% of pixels by 1. reference_env therefore returns the un-jitted function, which is the renderer as written. jax is a declared reference version because jax_threefry_partitionable selects between two threefry counter layouts that agree on 0 of 448 draws, and the night noise field is drawn from one of them.

resolution_consistency_applicability.all bands: not_applicable: the official renderer is itself resolution-inconsistent in every band -- world rows 0.4817 in full daylight and 0.0991 at night, strip rows 0.94 throughout, max abs 191 at S=10/2S=20
resolution_consistency_applicability.mechanisms: craftax.load_texture resamples every PNG with Image.NEAREST at each size, so 2S textures are not a 2x replication of the S ones; and the night noise field is drawn at the frame's own resolution

owed.Craftax.cuda_arm: The comparison arm ran on cpu. Craftax's render is the same torch gather on both devices (no CUDA-only fused kernel), but --device cuda is one flag and should be run on the GPU host with the Craftax GPU suites.
owed.PFRocketLanding.frames: Rocket renders only on cuda through nvdiffrast (CPU refusal is by design), so no frame was produced or compared on this host. OWED to the post-Wave-1 GPU oracle: the 200-state Step-7 reference corpus rendered at 480 px through both trees on one card in one job, byte-compared, plus tests/gpu for this cell. Everything the frame is a function of on the CPU side — the kinematics, the lagged camera, the float64 MVP, the material table, the scene arrays and the checker texture — IS compared here and is identical.
